stem: In which unit is capacitance measured?

options.content: The farad
options.rationale: Correct: the farad (F) is the unit of capacitance.

options.content: The ohm
options.rationale: The ohm is the unit of resistance.

options.content: The henry
options.rationale: The henry is the unit of inductance.

options.content: The ampere
options.rationale: The ampere is the unit of current.

explanation: Resistance: ohm. Capacitance: farad. Inductance: henry. Current: ampere.

stem: What is the main function of a diode?

options.content: To allow current to flow in one direction only
options.rationale: Correct: it conducts when forward biased and blocks the reverse direction.

options.content: To store charge and release it later
options.rationale: That is a capacitor.

options.content: To store energy in a magnetic field
options.rationale: That is an inductor.

options.content: To make the current in a circuit smaller by a fixed amount
options.rationale: That is the job of a resistor.

explanation: A diode has a low resistance in one direction and a very high resistance in the other.

stem: Which of these components is an active component?

options.content: A transistor
options.rationale: Correct: it can switch or amplify.

options.content: A resistor
options.rationale: A resistor is passive.

options.content: A capacitor
options.rationale: A capacitor is passive.

options.content: An inductor
options.rationale: An inductor is passive.

explanation: Resistors, capacitors and inductors are passive; diodes, transistors and ICs are active.

stem: A technician must measure the resistance of a resistor on a circuit board. What must be done first?

options.content: Connect the meter in series with the power supply
options.rationale: That is how current is measured.

options.content: Switch the circuit on and run it at full power
options.rationale: Measuring resistance with the power on gives false readings and can damage the meter.

options.content: Reverse the polarity of the supply
options.rationale: Resistors are not polarised and the supply is not needed.

options.content: Isolate it with the power off
options.rationale: Correct: other parts and the supply would otherwise give a false reading.

explanation: Resistance is measured with the power off and the component isolated.

stem: To measure the current through a lamp, where is the ammeter connected?

options.content: In parallel with the lamp across its two ends
options.rationale: A meter across the lamp measures voltage, and an ammeter there would act as a short circuit.

options.content: Across the battery terminals at all times
options.rationale: This would short the battery through the meter.

options.content: In series with the lamp
options.rationale: Correct: all of the current must pass through the meter.

options.content: Next to the lamp but not in the circuit
options.rationale: The meter must be part of the current path.

explanation: An ammeter has a very low resistance and is connected in series so the current passes through it.
hints: Current is measured by letting it flow through the meter.

stem: Rudo connects an LED directly to a 9 V battery without a resistor and it burns out at once. What is the reason?

options.content: The LED was connected in parallel with a capacitor
options.rationale: No capacitor was used.

options.content: The battery voltage was too low to light the LED
options.rationale: A voltage too low would give no light, not damage.

options.content: Nothing limited the current through the LED
options.rationale: Correct: an LED needs a series resistor to keep the current within its limit.

options.content: The LED needs an alternating current to work
options.rationale: An LED needs direct current in the forward direction.

explanation: An LED has a low resistance once it conducts, so the current is limited only by a series resistor.
hints: What does the resistor do in an LED circuit?

stem: How does a transistor act as a switch?

options.content: It stores charge on two plates and releases it later in short pulses
options.rationale: That is how a capacitor works.

options.content: A small base current controls a larger collector current
options.rationale: Correct: with no base current the transistor is off.

options.content: It lets current through only when the polarity of the supply is correct
options.rationale: That describes a diode.

options.content: It gives out light whenever current passes through it
options.rationale: That describes an LED.

explanation: The base current controls the collector current: no base current, no collector current.

stem: A 12 Ω resistor and a 4 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. Which statement about the combined resistance must be true?

options.content: It is 16 Ω because the resistances add
options.rationale: Adding is for series circuits.

options.content: It is less than 4 Ω
options.rationale: Correct: parallel resistance is always smaller than the smallest branch.

options.content: It is 8 Ω, the average of the two
options.rationale: The combined resistance is not the average.

options.content: It is 12 Ω, the larger of the two
options.rationale: It cannot be larger than the smallest branch.

explanation: In parallel, 1 ÷ R = 1 ÷ 12 + 1 ÷ 4 = 4 ÷ 12, so R = 3 Ω, smaller than 4 Ω.
hints: Extra branches give the current more paths.

stem: An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.
explanation: True. An inductor is a coil; the current in it creates a magnetic field which stores energy and opposes sudden changes of current.

stem: Resistance should be measured with the circuit switched on so that the meter has a supply to work with.
explanation: False. The meter has its own battery. The circuit must be off and the component isolated, otherwise the supply and other components affect the reading.

stem: Match each component to its function.

right.content: Stores energy in a magnetic field
Gives out light when current flows forward

explanation: Each component has a distinct role; the first three are passive and the last two are active.

stem: Complete Ohm's law.

payload.template: Voltage = {{blank:a}} × resistance. For a given voltage, a larger resistance gives a {{blank:b}} current. Resistances in series are {{blank:c}} to find the total.

explanation: V = I × R, so I = V ÷ R: more resistance, less current. Series resistances add.

stem: A 150 Ω resistor and a 250 Ω resistor are in series with a 6 V battery. Calculate the current in milliamperes.
Calculate the combined resistance of a 12 Ω resistor and a 4 Ω resistor connected in parallel.
An LED needs 2 V across it and a current of 10 mA (0.01 A). It is powered from a 5 V supply. Calculate the value of the series resistor.
workedSolution:
1. Voltage across the resistor = 5 − 2 = 3 V.
2. R = V ÷ I = 3 ÷ 0.01 = 300 Ω.
hints: The resistor takes the voltage that the LED does not.

stem: A current of 0.05 A flows through an 80 Ω resistor. Calculate the voltage across the resistor.
Explain how a transistor can be used as a switch to turn on a buzzer from a weak signal. [3]

points.description: The weak signal is applied to the base
A small base current allows a larger current to flow from collector to emitter
The larger current powers the buzzer; with no base current the buzzer is off

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The weak signal is connected to the base. A small base current lets a much larger current flow between collector and emitter through the buzzer. With no signal the transistor is off and the buzzer is silent.

explanation: Base signal, larger collector current, buzzer on or off.
hints: Name the three leads and say which current controls which.

stem: Describe how a technician uses a multimeter to test whether a fuse has blown. [4]

points.description: Switch off the power and remove the fuse
Set the multimeter to the continuity (or resistance) setting
Touch the probes to the two ends of the fuse
A buzzer or a very low reading shows the fuse is good; no buzzer or an infinite reading shows it has blown

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Switch off and remove the fuse. Set the meter to continuity and touch the probes to the two ends. A buzzer means the fuse is good; no buzzer means it has blown.

explanation: Isolate, set function, connect, interpret.

stem: State three safety precautions when soldering a component onto a circuit board. [3]

points.description: Place the hot iron in a stand when it is not in use
Work in a ventilated place so the fumes are not breathed in
Wear eye protection / unplug the iron when finished

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Keep the hot iron in its stand, work where there is good ventilation, and wear eye protection.

explanation: Any three valid precautions.
hints: Think about heat, fumes and eyes.

stem: A 12 V battery is connected to a 20 Ω resistor (R1) in series with two resistors in parallel: R2 of 30 Ω and R3 of 60 Ω.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the combined resistance of R2 and R3 in parallel.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total resistance of the circuit.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the current from the battery, in amperes.

parts.label: (d)
parts.explanation: R1 takes 6 V, leaving 6 V across each branch of the pair.
parts.workedSolution:
1. Voltage across R1 = 0.3 × 20 = 6 V.
2. The pair shares the remaining 12 − 6 = 6 V.
3. Voltage across R2 = 6 V.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: How does the current through R3 compare with the current through R2?

options.content: Larger
options.rationale: More resistance gives less current for the same voltage.

options.content: Equal
options.rationale: The currents are equal only if the resistances are equal.

options.content: Zero
options.rationale: Both branches carry current.

options.content: Smaller
options.rationale: Correct: R3 has the larger resistance and the same voltage.

parts.explanation: Same 6 V across both, but 60 Ω gives half the current of 30 Ω.

explanation: Parallel pair 20 Ω, total 40 Ω, current 0.3 A, voltage across the series resistor 6 V so 6 V across the pair.
hints: Combine the parallel pair first, then add the series resistor.
The parallel pair has the same voltage across each branch.

stem: A technician is repairing the power supply board of a school projector using a multimeter.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: How is the meter connected to measure the voltage across a component in a powered circuit?

options.content: In series with the component
options.rationale: That is how current is measured.

options.content: Between the mains and the fuse only
options.rationale: This is neither a standard test nor safe.

options.content: Across the component
options.rationale: Correct: voltage is measured in parallel.

options.content: Not connected: the meter is held near the component
options.rationale: The probes must make contact.

parts.explanation: Voltage is measured across (in parallel with) the component.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the multimeter setting that gives an audible sign that a wire or track is unbroken.
parts.explanation: The continuity setting beeps when the path is complete.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: A new electrolytic capacitor and a diode are to be fitted. Explain why their orientation matters.

points.description: Both are polarised, so they only work correctly one way round
Fitting them backwards can damage the component or the circuit

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A diode and an electrolytic capacitor are polarised. If they are fitted backwards the diode will not conduct as intended and the capacitor can be damaged.

parts.explanation: Polarity and the risk of damage.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State two safety precautions before removing a faulty component from the board.

points.description: Switch off and unplug the equipment
Allow capacitors to discharge / let hot parts cool

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Switch off and unplug the equipment, and wait for the capacitors to discharge and hot parts to cool.

explanation: Voltage is measured across a powered component, resistance and continuity with power off, and current in series.
hints: Which tests need the power off?
